chunks: And when Moses returned to his people, indignant and grieved, he said: 'How wickedly you behaved in my absence. Why must you hasten the decree of your Lord?' And he cast aside the tablets, and pulled his brother by the hair. 'O son of my mother,' said (Aaron), 'these people took advantage of my weakness and almost killed me. Do not let my enemies rejoice at my plight, and do not put me down among transgressors.'

key_terms.ابْنَ أُمَّ: O son of my mother (a term of endearment and respect)
key_terms.الظَّالِمِينَ: The transgressors or those who exceed bounds

ai.seo_question: What did Moses do when he returned to his people and found them worshipping the calf?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, Moses' casting of the Tablets signifies the temporary suspension of the Law due to the people's unworthiness, while his gripping Aaron's head by the hair (or beard) demonstrates paternal affection rather than anger, as Aaron had already died or was incapacitated. This event highlights the tension between divine authority and human frailty, with Aaron's plea 'do not make me with the wrongdoers' underscoring his desire to remain distinct from the idolaters despite his inability to stop them.
